sources.title: Roozbeh Hazrat, Graded Rings and Graded Grothendieck Groups (arXiv:1405.5071)
sources.locator: §1.2.2 shift of modules (1.16), printed pp.33–34; §1.2.4 and §1.2.6–1.2.9 graded free modules and the graded tensor product (1.21)–(1.23), printed pp.36–41 and 47–53; §2.3 graded Morita theory, printed pp.118–123 (Definition 2.3.3 p.118, Remark 2.3.4 p.119, Theorem 2.3.7 with proof pp.119–121, Theorem 2.3.8 pp.121–122, Example 2.3.9 p.123, Remark 2.3.10 p.123). No other part of the book was closely read.

contents.name: §1.2.2 (1.16): the α-suspension functor T_α: Gr-A→Gr-A, M↦M(α), is an isomorphism of categories with T_αT_β=T_{α+β}; (1.15) identifies homogeneous maps of degree α with graded maps M(−α)→N
§1.2.6 (1.21): M⊗N(α)=M(α)⊗N=(M⊗N)(α); (1.22): M⊗_A A(α)→M(α), m⊗a↦ma, is a graded isomorphism; (1.23): A(α)⊗_A A(β)≅A(α+β)

§1.2.4 and §1.2.9: the shifted regular modules A(γ) are graded free on one homogeneous generator, every graded module is a quotient of a graded free module, and graded projectives are summands of A^n(δ)
Definition 2.3.3: graded functors satisfy φT_α=T_αφ strictly; graded equivalences and associated graded functors on Mod-A are defined through the forgetful functor
Remark 2.3.4: graded functors are required to commute with suspensions, but natural transformations between them are not required to have that property

Theorem 2.3.7 with its proof: a graded equivalence φ: Gr-A→Gr-B is isomorphic to −⊗_A Q for a graded A–B-bimodule Q; the proof reconstructs the B-action on P=ψ(B) and the comparison Θ through the suspensions (2.13)–(2.16)
Theorem 2.3.8: graded Morita equivalence is equivalent to B≅gr End_A(P) for a graded A-progenerator P and to B≅gr eM_n(A)(δ)e for a homogeneous full idempotent e
contents.reason: The progenerator and homogeneous-idempotent characterizations of graded Morita equivalence belong to the Morita bicategories pair in this run; this page uses only the tensor-representation direction of Theorem 2.3.7 and does not build the reconstruction theory.

contents.name: Example 2.3.9: there are graded rings A,B with Gr-A≃Gr-B but not graded equivalent, because the equivalence functors need not commute with suspensions; the construction uses Dade's theorem for skew group rings
contents.reason: The skew-group-ring example illustrates the graded-versus-ungraded distinction but is not used by any proof on this pair, and its Dade-theorem machinery lies outside the homological-algebra scope; the pair's own B5 witnesses establish the necessity of the coherence restrictions by elementary computations.

contents.name: Remark 2.3.10: left-right symmetry of graded Morita theory and the special case in which all graded finitely generated projectives are graded free
contents.reason: The left-right symmetry statement and the graded-free classification are part of the Morita bicategories pair's content; this page fixes left modules and does not develop the opposite-hand theory or the graded-free classification.

sources.title: J. Fuchs, G. Schaumann, C. Schweigert, Eilenberg–Watts calculus for finite categories and a bimodule Radford S^4 theorem (arXiv:1612.04561v3)
sources.locator: Introduction, PDF pp.1–5 (classical Eilenberg–Watts statement for unital rings); §2.1, PDF pp.5–7, Lemmas 2.1–2.2 and Corollary 2.3; §2.10–2.11 existence of ends and coends, PDF p.13; §3.1, PDF pp.13–15, Definition 3.1 and the opening of the adjoint-equivalence triangle. Sections 3.2–5 were not used as proof suppliers.

contents.name: Introduction: classical Eilenberg–Watts for unital rings — a right exact functor preserving small coproducts is naturally isomorphic to tensoring with an S–R-bimodule, namely F(R_R) with its natural right R-action
contents.reason: The classical arbitrary-unital-ring statement is the subject of the in-run prerequisite pair eilenberg-watts-theorem-and-natural-transformations, which proves it with a complete local argument; this graded page cites that formulation only as the ungraded comparison and does not re-prove it.

contents.name: §2.1 Lemma 2.1: for finite-dimensional k-algebras, left exactness, existence of a left adjoint and representability Hom_A(M,−) are equivalent, and right exactness, existence of a right adjoint, G≅G(A)⊗_A− and G≅Hom_A(−,G(A)^*)^* are equivalent
contents.reason: These are the finite-dimensional-algebra variants of the Eilenberg–Watts correspondence, and the finite pair builds the right- and left-exact classification over finite categories; this page is the arbitrary graded-algebra statement and uses no finiteness.

contents.name: §2.1 Lemma 2.2 and Corollary 2.3: the equivalences Rex(A-mod,B-mod)≃(A-bimod-B)^op and Lex≃Rex, and the linear-functor formulation over finite linear categories
contents.reason: The categorical Eilenberg–Watts triangle between Deligne products and left or right exact functors is the Deligne-products pair's subject; this page classifies graded tensor functors by graded bimodules and introduces no Deligne product.

contents.name: §2.10–2.11 Corollary 2.10: existence of the ends and coends ∫_m F(m)⊗m and ∫^m F(m)⊗m for finite linear categories
contents.reason: Ends and coends over finite linear categories belong to the Deligne-products and Nakayama pair, which constructs the finite kernels explicitly; this page uses only homogeneous free presentations and does not introduce (co)ends.

contents.name: §3.1 Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.2: the abstract Eilenberg–Watts functors Φ^l,Ψ^l,Φ^r,Ψ^r giving adjoint equivalences A^op⊠B≃Lex(A,B) and ≃Rex(A,B)
contents.reason: The abstract finite-categorical Eilenberg–Watts triangle and its explicit (co)end formulas are proved in the Deligne-products pair; the graded theorem here is the module-level statement over graded algebras with coherent internal shifts.

contents.name: §4: the bimodule Radford S^4 theorem, relative Serre functors and module categories over finite tensor categories
contents.reason: The Radford S^4 theorem and relative Serre functors require finite tensor categories, exact module categories and bimodule categories, none of which is part of this pair; the design explicitly names them as outside scope and no item here depends on them.

sources.title: Alexander Kleshchev, Representation Theory of Symmetric Groups and Related Hecke Algebras (arXiv:0909.4844)
sources.locator: §2.2 'Graded representation theory', printed pp.6–8: the abelian category H-Mod of graded left modules with degree-preserving morphisms, the shift M⟨m⟩ with M⟨m⟩_n=M_{n−m}, and the graded Hom HOM_H(M,N)=⊕_n Hom_H(M⟨n⟩,N).

contents.name: §2.2: for a ℤ-graded F-algebra H, H-Mod is the abelian category of graded left H-modules with degree-preserving module homomorphisms as morphisms
§2.2 (2.3)–(2.4): the grading shift M⟨m⟩ with M⟨m⟩_n=M_{n−m}, with q^m[M]=[M⟨m⟩] and M⟨m⟩⊕-copies on the Grothendieck group
§2.2: HOM_H(M,N)=⊕_{n∈ℤ}Hom_H(M⟨n⟩,N) is the graded Hom of homogeneous maps, and degree-n maps are those carrying M_i into N_{i+n}
§2.2 Lemmas 2.1–2.3: radical and irreducibility of graded modules, and uniqueness of irreducible modules up to grading shift
contents.reason: These are structural results of modular representation theory over graded algebras with no bearing on the shift-coherence classification; no proof on this page uses radicals, graded irreducibles or q-composition multiplicities.

sources.title: M. Kamensky, Non-Commutative Algebra (BGU course notes, Spring 2017)
sources.locator: §5.1 'Functors between module categories', printed pp.47–57: categorical preliminaries on limits and colimits, Proposition 5.1.40, Theorem 5.1.43 with proof, Lemma 5.1.46, Corollary 5.1.48; §5.2 'Morita equivalence', printed pp.57–58 inspected for scope only.

contents.name: §5.1, printed p.53: arbitrary colimits are built from coproducts and cokernels, and additivity identifies coequalisers with cokernels of differences
contents.reason: The ungraded colimit-characterization lemma is already scaffolded by the in-run prerequisite pair, and the graded version on this page is proved independently from the corresponding published category-theory items, so the course-notes treatment is recorded as backing that earlier pair.

contents.name: Theorem 5.1.43 (Eilenberg–Watts): an additive functor between module categories is tensor representable if and only if it commutes with all colimits, equivalently with all quotients and direct sums; proof printed pp.54–57
contents.reason: This is the arbitrary-unital-ring theorem proved complete in the in-run prerequisite pair; the graded theorem here restricts F to graded modules and degree-zero maps and adds the coherent shift comparisons, so the ungraded statement is not re-proved.

contents.name: Proposition 5.1.44 and Lemma 5.1.46: a map of colimit-preserving functors is determined by its component at R, and componentwise isomorphism or vanishing propagates to every module
contents.reason: The determination of transformations by their component at the regular module is the ungraded counterpart of the local-smallness and classification arguments; the earlier pair already scaffolds it, and this page reproves the graded case through homogeneous free covers.

contents.name: Corollary 5.1.48: N↦F_N determines an equivalence from R–S-bimodules to colimit-preserving functors, with composition corresponding to tensor product of bimodules
contents.reason: The ungraded equivalence of hom-categories is the earlier pair's corollary; the graded version with coherent shifts and its bicategorical coherence are the content of this page and are proved from the graded associators rather than imported.

contents.name: §5.2: Morita equivalence of rings, invertible bimodules and the matrix-ring example
contents.reason: Morita equivalence, invertible bimodules and the matrix-ring example belong to the Morita bicategories pair, which builds directly on the ungraded Eilenberg–Watts theorem; this page's bicategorical corollary only needs the graded associator coherence.

sources.title: M. Khovanov and P. Seidel, Quivers, Floer Cohomology, and Braid Group Actions (arXiv:math/0006056)
sources.locator: §2a–2c, author pp.9–11: graded A_m-modules with degree-preserving maps, the self-equivalence {1} shifting the grading upwards by one, the homotopy category P(Q) of bounded complexes of projectives, the cochain shift [k] with M[k]^i=M^{k+i} and ∂_{M[k]}=(−1)^k∂_M, and the statement that {k} and [k] are quite different because objects of C_m are bigraded.

contents.name: §2a: A_m-mod is the category of graded modules with grading-preserving homomorphisms, and {1} is the self-equivalence shifting the grading upwards by one; indecomposable projectives are the P_i{k}
§2c: the cochain shift [k] has M[k]^i=M^{k+i} and ∂_{M[k]}=(−1)^k∂_M, and {k} and [k] are 'quite different' since the objects are bigraded abelian groups
§2c: P(Q) is the homotopy category of bounded complexes of projective objects of an abelian Q, with the mapping-cone convention ∂_{C(f)}(x,y)=(−∂_Mx,f(x)+∂_Ny)
contents.reason: The homotopy category of bounded complexes and its cone convention are the published bounded-bimodule-complexes page's setup; this page's derived remark uses those published theorems and does not redevelop complex or homotopy-category theory.

contents.name: §2b: the functors U_i and their Temperley–Lieb composition; bigradings determined up to overall shift
contents.reason: The Khovanov–Seidel braid-group actions and Temperley–Lieb realizations are specific to that paper's Floer-theoretic application and are not used by any item on this pair; only the shift conventions of §2a–2c are harvested.
